# Psalm 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.

**2** The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims His handiwork.

**3** Day after day pours out speech, and night after night reveals knowledge.

**4** There is no speech, nor are there words, whose voice is not heard.

**5** Their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. In them He has set a tent for the sun,

**6** which comes out like a bridegroom leaving his chamber, and, like a strong man, runs its course with joy.

**7** Its rising is from the end of the heavens, and its circuit to the end of them, and there is nothing hidden from its heat.

**8** The law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul; the testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple;

**9** the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes;

**10** the fear of the LORD is clean, enduring forever; the rules of the LORD are true, and righteous altogether.

**11** More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and drippings of the honeycomb.

**12** Moreover, by them is Your servant warned; in keeping them there is great reward.

**13** Who can discern his errors? Declare me innocent from hidden faults.

**14** Keep back Your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me! Then I shall be blameless, and innocent of great transgression.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **19:8-10**: Six synonyms for Torah, six adjectives, six effects — a perfect poetic structure. The Torah is described with the same grandeur as the heavens.

- **19:13-14**: The psalm moves from cosmic praise to personal confession — from the grandeur of the universe to the hidden faults of one human heart.

— LOGOS
